items.title: Chandhiok & Mahajan elevates Arveena Sharma to Partnership
items.summary: Chandhiok & Mahajan has elevated Arveena Sharma to its Partnership, further strengthening the firm's Restructuring & Insolvency practice and its leadership bench. Based in New Delhi, Sharma joins the partnership after more than 11 years of experience advising domestic and international clients on complex restructuring, insolvency, distressed acquisitions and special situations. Her practice also encompasses schemes of arrangement, corporate reorganisations, shareholder disputes, and matters relating to oppression and mismanagement. She has advised on several significant restructuring and insolvency mandates in India, including playing a key role in the resolution process of India's first airline insolvency under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. She has extensive experience representing resolution professionals, resolution applicants, financial and operational creditors, and corporate debtors across sectors including aviation, edtech, pharmaceuticals, real estate, manufacturing and financial services. items.title: Stamp duty on arbitral awards must exclude interest component: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently held that stamp duty on an arbitral award must be calculated on the principal amount awarded and not on the interest component even where such interest forms part of the total sum awarded by an arbitral tribunal. [ Patel KNR Infrastructure Ltd v. NHAI ] Justice Jasmeet Singh held that Section 23 of the Indian Stamp Act, 1899 makes it clear that the mere inclusion of an interest component in an instrument cannot result in an enhanced stamp duty liability. "The interest component cannot be included in the computation of stamp duty merely because it forms part of the total amount awarded by the Arbitral Tribunal," the Court observed. Justice Jasmeet Singh The Court delivered the ruling while dismissing a review petition filed by the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI) against an April 2024 order directing it to pay the balance interest due to Patel KNR Infrastructure Limited under an arbitral award. items.summary: Early Buddhism challenged existing social hierarchies, but how far did its ideas of equality extend?
